title: Senior production chef
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised
overviewOfRole: Overseeing the production of standardised dishes in a kitchen environment.
occupationalSummary: <p>Senior production chefs may work independently, taking full responsibility for a whole kitchen,&nbsp; lead team or may support the head chef in larger establishments. They report activities to the Head chef or appropriate line manager. They supervise production chef teams in a variety of kitchen environments, for example; schools, hospitals, the Armed Forces, care homes and high street casual dining or pub kitchens. Job roles include Head chef, Second Chef, Kitchen Manager / Supervisor, Cook. Senior production chefs have accountability for the day-to-day running of the kitchen service, producing, monitoring and maintaining consistent food standards, legislative requirements and quality across all areas and during all stages of production and supply.</p>

knowledges.detail: Business standards for production of all dishes on the menu.
Methods to monitor portioning, and presenting of food, to business standards.
Legislation and business standards for production of dishes to meet specific dietary requirements; religious, special, and allergenic.
Legislation and business standards for the storage of fresh, dried, tinned and frozen goods, following food safety procedures.
Procedures and techniques for opening and closing the kitchen, including handover.
How to find and use data to inform decision making about par levels.
Techniques to monitor and maintain food safety management systems to meet regulations e.g. Hazard Analysis Critical Control Points (HACCP) and Control of Substances Hazardous to Health (COSHH).
Food safety regulation and inspection process.
Health and safety legislation, regulations, guidelines and procedures relevant to own self and others, ensuring due diligence requirements are met.
Methods of monitoring the correct use and maintenance of food production equipment and the procedure for dealing with misuse and malfunctions.
Standard operating procedures used in the kitchen.
Sustainable working practices and systems to minimise overproduction.
Legislation related to waste management.
Methods to identify, plan for and minimise risks to kitchen service and operation.
Key performance indicators related to efficiency, performance, and profitability.
Techniques to ensure the fair and respectful treatment of all stakeholders, and ensure equity diversity and inclusion legislation is followed.
Performance criteria and feedback techniques to support others to meet performance expectations.
Techniques for maintaining good mental health and wellbeing, including asking for help with daily tasks and supporting others.
Professional standards including behaviour, appearance and timekeeping.
Principles of professional and effective communication during briefings, instructions and difficult conversations with stakeholders
Leadership and management approaches.
Recognise how all teams are dependent on each other and understand the importance of teamwork both back and front of house in achieving business objectives.
Principles of workload management.
The changes to menus, technology and trends relevant to the business and industry

behaviours.detail: Be diligent in ensuring safe and hygienic practises are followed.
Strive to achieve the required outcome and support positive, open communications that help  achieve the best result for customers and the business.
Be solution focussed when dealing with unexpected challenges.
Recognise personal growth and the achievement of colleagues.
Maintain a consistently positive and professional approach

skills.detail: Prepare and cook all dishes on the menu to business standards.
Portion and present food to business standards, correcting errors.
Prepare and cook dishes to meet specific dietary requirements; religious, special, and allergenic.
Monitor stock control, ordering, storage, and rotation.
Prepare and close down kitchen before and after service.
Use and analyse data to determine par levels.
Implement food safety management systems to meet regulations, including record keeping.
Monitor and ensure legislative compliance and the completion of due diligence documentation.
Monitor the correct use and maintenance of manual and electrical food-preparation and cooking tools, equipment, and technology, escalating malfunctions.
Monitor compliance with standard operating procedures in the kitchen.
Control resource allocation, using sustainable working practices and systems to minimise overproduction.
Control and minimise waste in compliance with legislation.
Risk assess situations, identifying and isolating matters of concern, establishing the cause, and intervene accordingly to minimise risk to people and organisation.
Focus production on meeting key performance targets related to efficiency, performance, and profitability.

Operate in a fair and respectful way, identifying and resolving any behaviours from staff or customers that adversely impact team members,  acknowledging that those with the protected characteristics outlined in equality legislation face additional barriers to fair and respectful treatment at work.
Use feedback techniques to support others to meet performance expectations.
Use techniques for maintaining good mental health and wellbeing, escalating concerns where appropriate.
Promote maintenance of professional standards to others.
Use professional communication methods during briefings, instructions and difficult conversations.
Maintain harmony with colleagues, identifying and dealing with problems constructively to drive a positive outcome.
Use workload management principles to plan, organise and prioritise.
Support the implementation of changes to menus and technology within the business

duties.dutyDetail: Oversee the production of dishes using fresh and pre-prepared ingredients
Oversee the production of dishes to meet specific dietary requirements; religious, special, and allergenic
Ensure compliance with standard operating procedures to produce and serve food to business standards
Monitor service to maintain efficiency and productivity of standard operating procedures
Oversee the correct storage and use of food stock, including the completion of relevant paperwork, and support with ordering
Ensure preparation and close down is undertaken to support daily customer demand
Monitor and maintain food safety management systems and ensure all food safety regulations are met
Oversee compliance with health and safety legislation, policies and procedures, including fire regulations
Oversee the safe and compliant preparation, use and cleaning of equipment
Oversee sustainability best practice in relation to the use of resources including energy, water and reduction and disposal of waste
Act to maintain service in the case of temporary disruption, changing plans as needed, to ensure the smooth running of kitchen operations
Plan, implement and review changes to procedures, equipment, or products within the kitchen environment
Meet key performance indicators related to performance, revenue, profit margins, and customer experience
Ensure compliance with  equity, diversity, inclusion and wellbeing guidelines and establish a supportive, inclusive and motivational working environment
Take personal responsibility for own development observing professional standards and acting on and giving feedback
